newsitem.title: USA: Moody's taps Boicourt to run state ratings group.
newsitem.headline: Moody's taps Boicourt to run state ratings group.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service has named Renee Boicourt to run the day-to-day operations of its state ratings group, moving long-time head George Leung to an expanded position, a spokeswoman for the rating agency said Monday.
Fran Lazerson said that the unpublicized move took place several weeks ago, with Boicourt, who used to report to Leung, now reporting directly to Doug Watson, head of the public finance group.
Lazerson added that Boicourt now manages the day-to-day activities of the state ratings group, which consists of three analysts.

Leung, meanwhile, is also reporting to Watson in a new position of senior representative with issuers and investors, according to Lazerson. In that capacity, Leung will still be involved with states and "high-profile" issuers, as well as with investors, she added.

Lazerson said that Leung will continue to be Moody's representative on the citizens budget committee for New York, and will take on new responsibility for Moody's relationship with the Public Securities Association, as well as speaking assignments.
Leung retained the title of vice president and managing director of the states and high-profile local ratings group, while Boicourt is a vice president and assistant director, Lazerson said.
